Summary: According to the sources, DRAGIN (Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models) achieved superior performance across all tested datasets and LLM variants, outperforming baseline methods and establishing new state-of-the-art results in dynamic RAG. The model's performance was particularly pronounced in multi-hop reasoning tasks. The EM and F1 scores for DRAGIN (Ours) were 0.309 and 0.3971 respectively, compared to 0.224 and 0.3076 for FLARE. DRAGIN outperformed other methods like SR-RAG, FL-RAG, FS-RAG, and Vicuna-13b-v1.5 wo-RAG across various datasets.
